 Luka Dončić, Austin Reaves, Matisse Thybulle, Ziaire Williams and Walker Kessler will start Wednesday’s game against the Warriors. 
 Dončić, Reaves and Kessler starting was expected since the summer, but there were questions as to who would complete the starting five. With Thybulle and Williams starting, defense has been prioritized, and both are worth watching in deeper fantasy leagues. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson 
 Source:  Los Angeles Lakers

 Collin Sexton (leg) will miss Wednesday’s season opener against the Warriors. 
 Sexton missed the preseason, and his Lakers debut will have to wait while he recovers from a right soleus strain. In Sexton’s absence, more minutes could be available for Ziaire Williams, Quentin Grimes and Bronny James. 
 Cameron Carr 
 LAL 
 Guard 
 #43 
 Cameron Carr (oblique) has been ruled out against the Warriors on Wednesday. 
 The rookie’s debut will have to wait a little longer. With Carr and Adou Thiero (knee) unavailable, Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams will be the primary wings available off the bench. 
 Adou Thiero 
 LAL 
 Guard 
 #1 
 Adou Thiero (knee) is out against the Warriors on Wednesday. 
 Knee issues continue to plague Thiero despite making some starts during the preseason. He won’t be available for the season opener, which should mean more minutes for Ziaire Williams and Matisse Thybulle on the wing. 
 Matisse Thybulle 
 LAL 
 Guard-Forward 
 #4 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that Matisse Thybulle has agreed to a one-year, $3.3 million deal to join the Los Angeles Lakers. 
 Thybulle brings much-needed depth to the new-look Lakers, and the three-and-D specialist should see meaningful minutes for LA. Over the last two seasons, he’s averaged 2.1 steals and shot 41.1% from beyond the arc. 
 Ziaire Williams 
 LAL 
 Forward 
 #1 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that the Lakers signed Ziaire Williams to a one-year, $3 million contract. 
 Despite averaging a career-high 10.2 points per game last season, Williams’ contract option was not picked up by the Nets. He will now join a Lakers roster that harbors ambitions of contending in the West, even with the LeBron James era ending. While he posted solid numbers over his two seasons in Brooklyn, Williams was still not reliable enough to be trusted in most fantasy leagues. That’s likely to remain the case in Los Angeles. 
 Ziaire Williams 
 BKN 
 Forward 
 #1 
 Hoopshype’s Michael Scotto reports that the Nets will decline Ziaire Williams’ option for the 2026-27 season. 
 Williams will become an unrestricted free agent after averaging 10.2 points for Brooklyn last season. The 24-year-old wing served as a part-time starter for the Nets over his two seasons with the team and still packs some upside as an NBA player. His fantasy impact at this point, however, isn’t anything more than an occasional streaming option for those fantasy managers who may need scoring. 
 Matisse Thybulle 
 POR 
 Guard-Forward 
 #4 
 Matisse Thybulle (ankle) is available to play against the Kings on Sunday. 
 Thybulle was listed as probable and has now officially been cleared to suit up. He has played a reserve role recently, which has led to plenty of defensive production over the past couple of weeks. 
 Matisse Thybulle 
 POR 
 Guard-Forward 
 #4 
 Matisse Thybulle (ankle) is probable for Sunday’s game against the Kings. 
 Thybulle sprained his right ankle during the first half of Friday’s win over the Clippers but returned after halftime. The probable tag suggests that he’ll be cleared to play in a game that the Trail Blazers need to win to secure the No. 8 seed in the West. A loss combined with a Clippers win over the Warriors would drop Portland to the No. 9 seed. 
 Matisse Thybulle 
 POR 
 Guard-Forward 
 #4 
 Matisse Thybulle (foot) is available to return to Friday’s game against the Clippers. 
 Thybulle tweaked something in his right foot before limping to the locker room in the first half. The Trail Blazers called him questionable to return at halftime, but now Thybulle is available to return. The 29-year-old small forward had three steals and two blocks in nine first half minutes. 
 Matisse Thybulle

 #4 
 Matisse Thybulle (foot) is questionable to return to Friday’s game against the Clippers. 
 Thybulle was everywhere on defense with three steals and two blocks in nine minutes off the bench in the first half, but tweaked something in his right foot and came up limping. At halftime, he was deemed questionable to return by the Trail Blazers. His absence doesn’t significantly impact Portland’s rotation.

 Brandon Miller had 18 points (7-of-21 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), two rebounds, one assist, one block and three three-pointers agains the Nets on Wednesday. 
 Miller had 18 points, but struggled with efficiency as he was 7-of-21 from the field and 3-of-14 from behind the three-point line. There will be better games in his future, but with Kon Knueppel and Coby White sidelined defenses will be continue to key on Miller.

 RJ Barrett 
 TOR 
 Forward-Guard

 Player Stats

 RJ Barrett amassed 20 points (8-of-14 FGs, 4-of-7 FTs), four rebounds and three assists in Wednesday’s win over the Bulls.
 After scoring six points on 3-of-8 shooting in the first half, Barrett scored 10 in the third quarter alone. He shot well on Wednesday, making just over half his shots, and he also posted solid rebound and assist numbers. Most encouraging were the 14 shots, possibly a sign that Barrett’s volume won’t suffer much with Kawhi Leonard back in Toronto. Barrett has long offered better value in points leagues than category leagues, and that’s unlikely to change in 2026-27. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Cam Boozer puts up 7 points (2-of-15 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), 10 rebounds, and 5 assists in NBA debut.
 Do not panic about the inefficient shooting. He will not shoot 13% from the field for the rest of his career. However, we saw why many fantasy managers were very excited to have him. He got 10 rebounds and 5 assists despite the bad shooting. If he made five more of those shots, it would be an incredible stat line.

 Ty Jerome leads the charge with 41 points (16-of-22 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), six rebounds, five assists, a block, and five 3-pointers in win against the Jazz.
 Ty Jerome led this team in shot attempts and was very efficient. The Jazz had no way to stop him, and he was the reason that this game got out of hand so early in the second quarter. He got into the paint whenever he wanted and took advantage of Jaren Jackson being in foul trouble. While he likely won’t continue to lead the team in shot attempts, he could be in line for a big year that could result in him having a top 50 fantasy season.

 Jakob Poeltl finished Wednesday’s win over the Bulls with three points (1-of-1 FGs, 1-of-3 FTs), six rebounds, one steal and one blocked shot.
 Four Raptors starters scored at least 20 points on Wednesday, with Poeltl (unsurprisingly) taking the hit. The 7-footer took only one shot, and low-attempt games will likely be the norm this season. Also, Collin Murray-Boyles (6/8/3/1/1) played 20 minutes off the bench, while Poeltl played 22. The two shared the court for three minutes during the first quarter, but that was it. If Poeltl and CMB split minutes evenly as the season progresses, the former may not be worth rostering in 12-team leagues. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Grayson Allen had 21 points (6-of-9 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), three rebounds, four assists, one steal and five three-pointers against the Nets on Wednesday. 
 With Kon Knueppel (hamstring) sidelined, the Hornets need Sion James and Allen to pick up the slack. James started, but scored just three points in 26 minutes. Meanwhile, Allen had 21 points and five three-pointers in 28 minutes off the bench. Allen is the preferred streaming option while Knueppel is sidelined. 
 -  Nick Shlain

 Scottie Barnes 
 TOR

 Player Stats

 Scottie Barnes accounted for 23 points (8-of-19 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), six rebounds, five assists and one three-pointer in Wednesday’s win over the Bulls.
 Wednesday was a record night in Toronto, as the Raptors broke last season’s mark for the largest season-opening win in franchise history. In the 135-92 rout of the Bulls, Barnes also moved into fifth on the franchise’s all-time assist list, passing Pascal Siakam. “Scottie B” was one of four Raptors starters to finish with at least 20 points, and he led the team in shot attempts (19). This sets up to be another big fantasy season for Barnes, especially with Kawhi Leonard making his return to Toronto. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Naz Reid

 #0

 Naz Reid had 20 points (8-of-18 FGs, 0-of-1 FTs), 11 rebounds, seven assists and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s 110-103 victory over the Nets. 
 Reid impressed in his first game with the Hornets. The 27-year-old big man led the team with 20 points, knocked down four three-pointers and was just three assists shy of a triple-double. That’ll play. Reid has never averaged more than 2.2 assists in a season, but the rest of his production is sustainable, making him a valuable player in the middle rounds of fantasy drafts. 
 -  Nick Shlain
